posts.title: Healey says borrowing costs have risen £14bn this year
posts.text: Healey says economists talk of headwinds. But Britain is facing storms. The war in Iran has caused turmoil, he says. He says the government did not want the war, and ignored Kemi Badenoch’s invitation to jump in. Inflation has gone up, oil prices have gone up, and gas prices have nearly tripled since February. This…

Healey says it is an honour to be delivering the budget. He jokes that he hoped to be the most watched minister this week – until the PM went on Gogglebox. And he pays tribute to his predecessor Rachel Reeves. She was the first female chancellor and restored economic credibility, he says.

Ghani calls John Healey – mistakenly calling him “Sir John”. Healey starts by saying this is a budget for the working people of Britain. He says: This is a budget for the working people of Britain. For British businesses, big and small. Delivered at a time when global uncertainties and pressures are swirling worldwide…
PMQs is over. Lindsay Hoyle is now vacating his seat, because by tradition the deputy speaker takes the chair for the budget statement. Nusrat Ghani is now in charge of proceedings.
Josh Newbury (Lib Dem) asks if the government will take more action on press regulation. Burnham says press intrusion can be unacceptable. He offers to hold a meeting with Newbury on this.

posts.title: Burnham says using North Sea reserves can 'accelerate' move to a 'clean energy future'
posts.text: Danny Kruger (Reform UK) asks Burnham if he confirms the budget numbers assume that the Rosebank oilfield will be allowed. (See 10.25am.) Burnham says the Rosebank decision is a quasi-judicial decision that will be taken by the energy secretary. But he says Kruger is right to say the use of the UK’s North Sea reserves…
Dave Robertson (Lab) says Royal Mail has a problem because it cannot compete with competitor companies that don’t give their workers equivalent rights. Burnham says he will look at this issue.

posts.title: Burnham ducks invitation to condemn Steve Witkoff for calling Putin a humanitarian
posts.text: Johanna Baxter (Lab) asks if Burnham agrees that Steve Witkoff, Donald Trump’s envoy, was wrong to call President Putin a humanitarian. She says: The people of my constituency looked on in horror that our closest ally could use such words for a man wanted by the international criminal court for the systematic…

Davey asks Burnham if he will back the UK joining the EU single market and customs union. Burnham says he wants to get a better relationship. And he says it is “extraordinary” that the Tories do not support trying to improve the Brexit deal.

Ed Davey, the Lib Dem leader, says he welcomes the news that the carer’s allowance cliff-edge will be abolished. But he says he is not happy about the details. He says: It won’t take effect for four years and, when it does, the government will claw back £1 for every £1 a carer earns – a 100% tax rate for working…
Burnham says he is “increasingly confident” that he will be able to meet his target of ensuring that all rough sleepers get the offer of a bed for the night before the end of the year.

Badenoch asks Burnham to rule out any referendum on the EU or the single market. Burnham says he is “doing what I can do to get a better deal for Britain”. That is part of his job, he says. He says the CBI and other business organisations and big businesses support his drive to get a better deal.

Badenoch claims Brexit has been good for London. Does Burnham really think the country wants to reopen the Brexit debate. She says Burnham was not in parliament at the time. The country was paralysed. It was miserable, regardless of which side of the debate you were on. Yes, says Burnham. He claims Badenoch has…
